How vaccines train the immune system

By Jane Roe, 5 min read

A vaccine works by showing the body a harmless piece of a germ so that the immune system can learn to recognise it later.

When the real germ arrives, the antibodies that were made earlier can quickly attack it before it has a chance to spread.

Why boosters matter

Over time the number of antibodies in the blood goes down, which is why some vaccines need a booster dose to keep the protection strong.

Vaccines prevent millions of deaths every year according to estimates from the major health agencies.
